question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
It is a misconception that the more you learn, the more likely you are to succeed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Certainty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Misconception" means a view or opinion that is incorrect, based on faulty thinking or understanding (गलत धारणा). Its antonym should express a correct, sure, and accurate understanding.

• "Certainty" means the state of being completely confident that something is true (निश्चितता), which is the exact opposite of holding a mistaken or false belief.
◦ Example: She spoke with certainty about the results of the experiment, having verified them thoroughly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Illusion" (भ्रम): A false idea or belief; a synonym, not an antonym, of misconception.

• Option 2: "Hallucination" (मतिभ्रम): An experience of perceiving something that does not actually exist; again a synonym of a false perception, not its opposite.

• Option 3: "Fallacy" (भ्रांति): A mistaken belief, especially one based on unsound argument; this too is close in meaning to misconception, not opposite to it.

NOTE

• Words like illusion, delusion, fallacy, hallucination and misconception all cluster around the idea of a false belief or perception and are frequently used as synonyms for one another in SSC vocabulary questions.

• Common antonym pairs tested by SSC: fact ↔ fallacy, reality ↔ illusion, certainty ↔ doubt/misconception, truth ↔ myth.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Colleague
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Co-worker.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Colleague" means a person with whom one works, especially in a profession or business (सहकर्मी).

• "Co-worker" carries the same meaning — a fellow worker or employee who works with someone in the same organisation.
◦ Example: She invited all her colleagues to the office party after finishing the project with her co-workers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Consult" (परामर्श करना): To seek information or advice from someone; a verb, unrelated in meaning to "colleague".

• Option 3: "Distend" (फुलाना): To swell or bulge out, usually used for a part of the body; completely unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: "Exempt" (छूट प्राप्त): Free from an obligation or liability; also unrelated in meaning to "colleague".

NOTE

• Other common synonyms of "colleague" tested by SSC: associate, peer, teammate, collaborator.

• Do not confuse colleague (a co-worker) with college (an educational institution) — a very common spelling confusion in SSC papers.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
All the employees feel that continuing working there is perilous to their careers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Dangerous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Perilous" means full of danger or risk; hazardous (खतरनाक).

• "Dangerous" means likely to cause harm or injury, which is exactly synonymous with perilous.
◦ Example: Climbing the icy cliff without proper gear was a perilous, dangerous undertaking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Convenient" (सुविधाजनक): Fitting in well with a person's needs or plans; opposite in tone to "perilous".

• Option 3: "Helpful" (सहायक): Giving or ready to give help; unrelated in meaning to "perilous".

• Option 4: "Suitable" (उपयुक्त): Right or appropriate for a particular purpose; unrelated in meaning to "perilous".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "perilous" frequently asked by SSC: hazardous, risky, precarious, treacherous, unsafe.

• Its antonym is "safe" or "secure", also commonly tested.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that contains the error. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
Nobody from the gathering of odd people could guess the accident occurring blast.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the accident occurring blast.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "the accident occurring blast" is grammatically faulty. A noun "blast" cannot be modified by stacking two nouns/participles ("accident" and "occurring") in this awkward order — the intended meaning is "the blast that occurred due to the accident" or "the accidental blast/explosion".

• Rule — Modifying a noun: When we want to describe a noun with the reason or cause behind it, we either use a relative clause ("the blast that occurred due to the accident") or a single appropriate adjective ("the accidental blast"). Using a noun ("accident") directly before a present participle ("occurring") followed by another noun ("blast") produces an ungrammatical, confusing string of modifiers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Nobody from the gathering" is grammatically correct — "nobody" is a correct singular indefinite pronoun and "from the gathering" is a correctly formed prepositional phrase.

• Option 3: "No error" is incorrect because an error does exist, in segment 1.

• Option 4: "of odd people could guess" is grammatically correct — "of odd people" correctly modifies "gathering", and "could guess" is a correctly formed modal + base verb construction.

NOTE

• In error-spotting questions, always check whether a string of nouns/participles before another noun makes logical, grammatical sense — this is a favourite SSC trap.

• When in doubt, try to say the sentence aloud in a natural way; an unnatural pile-up of nouns before the head noun is usually the error.

question:
Select the most appropriate homonym in the context of the following sentence to fill in the blank.
The key was hanging on a ________by the door.
option_1: nail: to catch someone, especially when they are doing something wrong, or guilty
option_2: nail: a small metal spike, driven into wood to join things together or to serve as a hook
option_3: nail: a thin, hard area that covers the upper side of the end of each finger and each toe
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. nail: a small metal spike, driven into wood to join things together or to serve as a hook.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence **"The key was hanging on a ________ by the door"** requires a physical object on which a key can be hung.

• Among the different meanings ("homonyms") of the word "nail", the sense that fits here is "a small metal spike, driven into wood to join things together or to serve as a hook" — a key can literally be hung on such a nail fixed in a wall or door frame.
◦ Example: He hammered a nail into the wall and hung his coat on it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "nail: to catch someone, especially when they are doing something wrong, or guilty" — this is the verb sense of "nail" (as in "to nail someone"), which does not fit the context of hanging a key.

• Option 3: "nail: a thin, hard area that covers the upper side of the end of each finger and each toe" — this is the anatomical sense (fingernail/toenail), which does not fit the sentence.

• Option 4: "nail: to do something successfully" — this is another verb sense (as in "to nail a performance"), which does not fit the context.

NOTE

• A word that has the same spelling and pronunciation but different, unrelated meanings is called a homonym (e.g. bat, bank, spring, nail).

• Always identify the part of speech required by the sentence (here, a noun naming a physical object) before choosing among the homonym's meanings.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Surrugocy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Surrogacy" — the practice of a woman carrying and giving birth to a child on behalf of another person or couple.
◦ Example: The couple decided to have a child through surrogacy after years of failed treatment.

• Spelling key: SUR + ROGA + CY. The word is spelt S-U-R-R-O-G-A-C-Y; the printed form "Surrugocy" wrongly changes the second syllable "ro" to "ru" and the fourth syllable "ga" to "go".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Obdurate" is correctly spelt — it means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion.

• Option 2: "Cryptic" is correctly spelt — it means having a meaning that is mysterious or not easily understood.

• Option 4: "Drastic" is correctly spelt — it means likely to have a strong or far-reaching effect.

NOTE

• Related word: "Surrogate" (a substitute, or a person who carries a pregnancy for another), from which "surrogacy" is derived.

• Other commonly misspelt SSC words with doubled letters/tricky vowels: accommodate, embarrass, occurrence, questionnaire, harass.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(P) and the impact of their
(Q) the authors' journey of self-discovery
(R) the memoir explores
(S) upbringing on their identity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. RQPS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A meaningful sentence must begin with a clear subject and verb, and every pronoun/possessive used later must have a clear antecedent already introduced.

• Part (R) "the memoir explores" is the natural opening, giving the subject ("the memoir") and main verb ("explores"). It must be followed by its object, part (Q) "the authors' journey of self-discovery", since "explores" needs an object.

• Part (P) "and the impact of their" logically continues after (Q), joining a second object to "explores" with "and"; the possessive "their" in (P) correctly refers back to "the authors'" introduced in (Q). Finally, part (S) "upbringing on their identity" completes the phrase begun in (P) — "the impact of their upbringing on their identity".
◦ Full sentence: The memoir explores the authors' journey of self-discovery and the impact of their upbringing on their identity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: RQSP is incorrect because it places (S) "upbringing on their identity" directly after (Q), which breaks the required sequence "impact of their upbringing".

• Option 3: QPSR is incorrect because it begins with (Q), leaving "the authors' journey of self-discovery" without an introducing subject-verb ("the memoir explores"), and stacks the verb (R) at the end where it does not fit grammatically.

• Option 4: SPRQ is incorrect because it begins with (S), which starts mid-phrase ("upbringing on their identity") without any subject or verb preceding it, making the opening meaningless.

NOTE

• In sentence-rearrangement (para-jumble) questions, first identify the part that supplies the main subject and finite verb — that part almost always opens the sentence.

• Track possessive pronouns like "their", "his", "its" — they must always follow the noun they refer back to.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
I have read that / a Leaning Tower of Pisa is a / popular tourist attraction / in the world.
option_2: a Leaning Tower of Pisa is a
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a Leaning Tower of Pisa is a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "a Leaning Tower of Pisa is a" contains a grammatical error: the proper noun "Leaning Tower of Pisa" is a unique, specific landmark and must take the definite article "the", not the indefinite article "a". The correct form is "the Leaning Tower of Pisa is a...".

• Rule — Articles with proper nouns: Unique landmarks, monuments and famous structures (e.g. the Taj Mahal, the Eiffel Tower, the Leaning Tower of Pisa) always take the definite article "the", since there is only one of them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "I have read that" is grammatically correct — the Present Perfect Tense ("have read") is correctly used with the connector "that" introducing the noun clause that follows.

• Option 3: "popular tourist attraction" is grammatically correct — a correctly formed adjective + noun phrase.

• Option 4: "in the world" is grammatically correct — a correctly formed prepositional phrase completing the sentence.

NOTE

• The definite article "the" is compulsorily used before: names of rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges, famous buildings/monuments, and superlatives (e.g. the Ganga, the Himalayas, the Red Fort, the best).

• The indefinite article "a/an" is used only for a non-specific, one-of-many noun, never for a unique landmark.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Devil's advocate
option_1: One who takes an opposing position for the sake of argument
option_2: One who presents very logical arguments
option_3: One who is very precise and accurate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. One who takes an opposing position for the sake of argument.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Devil's advocate" means a person who deliberately argues against or takes an opposing side of an issue, not because they believe it, but to test the strength of the original argument or to encourage debate (जान-बूझकर विरोधी पक्ष रखने वाला व्यक्ति).
◦ Example: I don't really disagree with the plan; I'm just playing devil's advocate to make sure we've considered every risk.

• The phrase originates from a former official position in the Roman Catholic Church whose job was to argue against a candidate's canonisation, to ensure the case for sainthood was rigorously tested.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "One who presents very logical arguments" describes a rational or logical person in general, not specifically someone who deliberately takes the opposing side.

• Option 3: "One who is very precise and accurate" describes a meticulous person, unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

• Option 4: "One who never argues" is the opposite of a devil's advocate, who by definition does argue (deliberately, against the prevailing view).

NOTE

• Other idioms about arguments/debate frequently asked by SSC: "To play devil's advocate" (same meaning), "To split hairs" (to argue over unimportant details), and "To agree to disagree" (to accept differing opinions without further argument).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
The doctor assured the patient that the tumour was benign and could be easily removed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Malignant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Benign" means (especially of a tumour) not harmful in effect; not cancerous or dangerous (सौम्य / हानिरहित).

• "Malignant" means (of a tumour) tending to invade normal tissue or recur after removal; cancerous and dangerous (घातक), which is the exact medical opposite of "benign".
◦ Example: Further tests confirmed that, unlike the earlier benign growth, this tumour was malignant and required immediate treatment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Favourable" (अनुकूल): Expressing approval or support; not the specific medical opposite of "benign".

• Option 3: "Sterile" (बाँझ / कीटाणुरहित): Free from germs, or unable to reproduce; unrelated in meaning to "benign".

• Option 4: "Kind" (दयालु): Having a friendly, generous nature; this is actually closer to a general synonym of "benign" (in its non-medical sense of "gentle, kindly"), not its antonym.

NOTE

• "Benign" has two common senses in SSC vocabulary: (i) gentle/kindly (opposite: cruel/malicious) and (ii) medically harmless (opposite: malignant). Context (here, "tumour") decides which sense is intended.

• Related medical opposites often tested: benign ↔ malignant, acute ↔ chronic, curable ↔ terminal.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The director hired the new employee after the interview.
option_1: The new employee will be hired by the director after the interview.
option_2: The new employee was hired by the director after the interview.
option_3: The new employee is being hired by the director after the interview.
option_4: The new employee hired by the director after the interview.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The new employee was hired by the director after the interview.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The active sentence "The director hired the new employee after the interview" is in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the new employee" becomes the subject; since it is singular, the auxiliary used is "was"; the verb "hired" becomes its past participle form "hired" (V3, same as V2 here); and "the director" becomes the agent after "by".
◦ Passive: The new employee was hired by the director after the interview.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will be hired" is the future passive form, but the original sentence is in the simple past tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "is being hired" is the passive of the Present Continuous Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

• Option 4 is incorrect because the auxiliary verb "was" has been dropped ("hired" alone cannot function as the passive verb without an auxiliary), making the sentence grammatically incomplete.

NOTE

• Always match the tense of the passive auxiliary to the tense of the original active sentence — a very common SSC trap is offering a passive in the wrong tense.

• The time expression "after the interview" remains unchanged and is simply carried over to the end of the passive sentence.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A.That the only true individual
B.Is the holy man
C.It has frequently been claimed
D.Which the traditional society of India tolerates
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. C, A, D, B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part (C) "It has frequently been claimed" is the natural opening, since it introduces the impersonal reporting structure "It has been claimed that...", which needs a noun clause (introduced by "that") to follow.

• Part (A) "That the only true individual" supplies exactly this noun clause, beginning with "that" and introducing the subject "the only true individual", which itself needs to be further defined.

• Part (D) "Which the traditional society of India tolerates" is a relative clause that correctly modifies "the only true individual" from (A), describing which individual is meant. Part (B) "Is the holy man" then supplies the main verb "is" and complement for the subject "the only true individual", completing the sentence.
◦ Full sentence: It has frequently been claimed that the only true individual which the traditional society of India tolerates is the holy man.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: D, C, A, B is incorrect because it begins with the relative clause (D), which cannot stand without the noun ("the only true individual") it is meant to modify.

• Option 3: A, B, D, C is incorrect because it places the verb-complement (B) immediately after (A), before the relative clause (D) has identified which individual is being discussed, and ends on the reporting clause (C), which cannot come last.

• Option 4: C, D, A, B is incorrect because it inserts the relative clause (D) immediately after (C), before the noun clause "that the only true individual" (A) that (D) is supposed to modify has even been introduced.

NOTE

• When a sentence opens with an impersonal reporting phrase like "It has been said/claimed/argued that...", look for the part beginning with "that" to follow it directly.

• Relative pronouns like "which", "who", "that" must always come immediately after the noun they describe.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.
Drunkeness, riot and brawling were the order, there, every night.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Drunkeness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Drunkenness" — the state of being intoxicated with alcohol.
◦ Example: Public drunkenness was strictly punished under the new municipal law.

• Spelling key: DRUNKEN + NESS. The base word "drunken" already ends in "-n", and the suffix "-ness" is simply added to it, giving a double "n" — D-R-U-N-K-E-N-N-E-S-S. The printed form "Drunkeness" wrongly drops one of the two "n"s.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Riot" is correctly spelt — it means a violent disturbance of the peace by a crowd.

• Option 3: "Order" is correctly spelt — here used in the sense of the normal, established way of things.

• Option 4: "Brawling" is correctly spelt — it means engaging in a rough or noisy fight/quarrel.

NOTE

• A common SSC spelling trap is a double consonant lost when a suffix is added to a word already ending in that consonant — e.g. drunken + ness = drunkenness, thin + ness = thinness, suddenness, meanness.

• Do not confuse "drunkenness" (the state of being drunk) with "drunkard" (a person who is habitually drunk).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
Can you please make sure that all the guest are gathered on the stage before the performance begins?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. guests are gathered by.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment "guest are gathered on" contains a subject-verb agreement error: the subject "all the guest" is plural in sense (preceded by "all the"), so the noun must be "guests" (plural) to agree with the plural auxiliary verb "are".

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: A plural subject (indicated here by the quantifier "all") must always be followed by a plural noun and a plural verb form — "all the guests are...", never "all the guest are...".

• Among the grammatically correct options, "guests are gathered by" correctly uses the plural noun "guests" with the plural auxiliary "are", and the preposition "by" is an acceptable choice of location marker ("gathered by the stage").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "guest is gathered on" is incorrect because it retains the singular, ungrammatical "guest" and pairs it with the singular auxiliary "is", which cannot follow "all the".

• Option 2: "guests are gathered in" corrects the noun and verb agreement but uses the preposition "in", which is not idiomatic with "the stage" (a stage is a platform, not an enclosed space one can be gathered "in").

• Option 4: "guests is gathered by" corrects the noun to the plural "guests" but wrongly retains the singular auxiliary "is", again violating subject-verb agreement.

NOTE

• The quantifier "all" before a countable noun always requires the plural form of that noun (all the guests, all the students, all the books).

• Common preposition confusions tested by SSC: in/on/at with places — "on the stage/platform", "in the hall/room", "at the venue".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Spill the beans
option_1: Open the flow of the stopped water
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Disclose the secrets accidentally.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Spill the beans" means to reveal secret or confidential information, often without meaning to or before the proper time (राज़ खोल देना).
◦ Example: He accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party while talking to his sister.

• The expression is believed to originate from an ancient Greek voting method using coloured beans, where an accidentally overturned jar would prematurely reveal the (secret) result of the vote.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Open the flow of the stopped water" is a literal description unrelated to the figurative meaning of the idiom.

• Option 2: "Liberate the controlled emotions" describes releasing pent-up feelings, which is a different idiom altogether ("to let off steam"), not "spill the beans".

• Option 3: "Distribute food grains freely" is a literal, unrelated meaning that has nothing to do with revealing information.

NOTE

• Other idioms of revealing/keeping secrets often asked by SSC: "To let the cat out of the bag" (same meaning as spill the beans), "To keep something under wraps" (to keep secret), and "To be tight-lipped" (to refuse to reveal information).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined segment in the following sentence.
The king's coronation ceremony was a grand affair, with all the nobles and dignitaries dressed in their finest insignia of royalty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Regalia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "insignia of royalty" refers to the ceremonial emblems, symbols and paraphernalia associated with a king or royal office (such as the crown, sceptre, and royal robes).

• "Regalia" (राजसी वस्त्र/चिह्न) is the precise one-word substitute for this — it specifically means the emblems, symbols, or costumes that are the distinctive sign of royalty or high office.
◦ Example: The king appeared before his subjects dressed in full regalia, wearing his crown and ceremonial robes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Ornaments" (आभूषण): General decorative items or jewellery, not specifically the emblems of royal office.

• Option 3: "Regals": Not a standard English word in this sense; "regal" is only an adjective meaning "of or fit for a king", and has no such noun form.

• Option 4: "Spectres" (भूत/प्रेत): Ghosts or apparitions; entirely unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions frequently tested: "Coronation" (the ceremony of crowning a king or queen), "Abdicate" (to formally give up the throne), "Monarchy" (government by a king or queen).

• Do not confuse "regalia" (royal emblems/attire) with "regatta" (a boat race).

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A.The post-COVID period has caused many asymptomatic diseases.
B.Though it cannot be believed for sure; the change in social life may be a major cause.
C.These are people who suffered infection once or never at all.
D.Some propose that survival post infection has changed the mindset of people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A, C, D, B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part (A) "The post-COVID period has caused many asymptomatic diseases" is the natural topic-opening sentence, introducing the subject of the paragraph — asymptomatic diseases caused after COVID.

• Part (C) "These are people who suffered infection once or never at all" logically follows (A), using the pronoun "These" to refer back to the people affected by these asymptomatic diseases mentioned in (A).

• Part (D) "Some propose that survival post infection has changed the mindset of people" then offers one possible explanation for the phenomenon just described. Part (B) "Though it cannot be believed for sure; the change in social life may be a major cause" logically closes the paragraph, using "though" to add a qualifying, alternative explanation to the one proposed in (D).
◦ Full paragraph: The post-COVID period has caused many asymptomatic diseases. These are people who suffered infection once or never at all. Some propose that survival post infection has changed the mindset of people. Though it cannot be believed for sure, the change in social life may be a major cause.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: B, D, C, A is incorrect because it opens with "Though it cannot be believed for sure", a qualifying clause that has no preceding statement to qualify.

• Option 2: B, D, A, C is incorrect for the same reason — it opens with the qualifying clause (B) before any claim has been made, and additionally separates (A) from the pronoun "These" in (C) that refers to it.

• Option 4: A, C, B, D is incorrect because it places the qualifying clause (B) before the proposed explanation (D) that it is meant to qualify, reversing the logical cause-and-alternative sequence.

NOTE

• In paragraph-jumble questions, track pronouns and demonstratives ("these", "it", "this") — they must be placed immediately after the noun/idea they refer to.

• Words like "though", "however", "but" signal a qualifying or contrasting idea and rarely open a paragraph unless a claim has already been made.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
She was completely baffled by his strange behaviour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Confused.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Baffled" means completely bewildered or puzzled; unable to understand or explain something (हैरान/असमंजस में).

• "Confused" means unable to think clearly or understand something, which is synonymous with "baffled" in this context.
◦ Example: She was completely baffled/confused by the strange noises coming from the attic.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Unfazed" (अविचलित): Not disconcerted or worried; this is actually close to the opposite of "baffled" (unfazed = unbothered, composed).

• Option 3: "Relieved" (राहत महसूस करना): No longer feeling anxious or distressed; unrelated to the meaning of "baffled".

• Option 4: "Angered" (क्रोधित): Made angry; a different emotion altogether from confusion/bewilderment.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "baffled" frequently tested: puzzled, perplexed, bewildered, mystified, confounded.

• Its antonym is typically "enlightened" or "clear(-headed)".

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The speech of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam influences young minds.

option_2: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Young minds were influenced by the speech of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Young minds are influenced by the speech of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The active sentence "The speech of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam influences young minds" is in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V1/V5 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "young minds" becomes the subject; being plural, it takes the auxiliary "are"; the verb "influences" becomes its past participle "influenced"; and "the speech of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam" becomes the agent after "by".
◦ Passive: Young minds are influenced by the speech of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "get influenced" is a loosely-formed passive that also omits the original subject "the speech of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam" as the agent, and does not correctly mirror the simple present passive structure.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "were influenced" is the passive of the Simple Past Tense, not the Simple Present Tense used in the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it changes the sentence structure entirely, making "the speech" the subject and using the awkward construction "is very influencing", which is not a correct passive form and also misspells "Abdul" as "Adul".

NOTE

• Sentences with an inanimate/abstract subject acting on people (e.g. "the speech influences young minds") are commonly tested for passive conversion — the process is identical to any other Simple Present sentence.

• Always double-check the auxiliary verb matches the number (singular/plural) of the new subject after conversion.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
One who possesses outstanding technical ability in a particular art or field
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Virtuoso.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "One who possesses outstanding technical ability in a particular art or field" describes a highly skilled expert, especially in a fine art such as music.

• "Virtuoso" (कलाविद्/निपुण कलाकार) is the precise one-word substitute — it means a person highly skilled in some art, especially music; a person with masterly ability, technique, or personal style.
◦ Example: The pianist was hailed as a virtuoso after his flawless performance of the difficult concerto.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Virtuous" (सदाचारी): Having or showing high moral standards; describes moral character, not technical skill — a common confusable pair with "virtuoso".

• Option 3: "Gourmand" (पेटू): A person who is fond of, and often greedy about, eating and drinking; unrelated to technical skill.

• Option 4: "Amateur" (शौकिया): A person who engages in a pursuit without professional skill or training; the near opposite of a virtuoso.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the sound-alike pair "virtuous" (morally good) and "virtuoso" (technically brilliant in an art) — this is a very common SSC trap.

• Related one-word substitutions: "Connoisseur" (an expert judge in matters of taste, especially in the fine arts), "Maestro" (a distinguished figure in music, especially a conductor).

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Following in the footsteps of France, Italy has ________(1)________ a new tax to be ________(2)________ on large tech companies, a move that is likely to put more strain on the country's relations with the USA. The Italian parliament has approved a 3% digital tax on some digital revenue of technology companies that make over $831 million in global revenue, including at least $6 million in Italy. The tax ________(3)________ similar to the one France implemented earlier this year, which has attracted ________(4)________ criticism from the USA. According to a report in The Epoch Times, dozens of countries are working on proposals to change corporate tax schemes to ________(5)________ money from tech firms that have users across the world, such as Facebook and Google's parent company Alphabet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. approved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a verb describing what Italy has done with "a new tax", in the Present Perfect Tense ("Italy has ________ a new tax").

• The passage itself later confirms this action explicitly: "The Italian parliament has approved a 3% digital tax..." — so the verb "approved" is both grammatically correct (a valid past participle after "has") and confirmed by the context of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "accepted" does not fit the specific legislative context described later in the passage, which explicitly uses the word "approved".

• Option 2: "declined" means to refuse or reject, which contradicts the rest of the passage describing the tax being implemented.

• Option 4: "favoured" means to support or prefer, which does not match the formal legislative action ("the Italian parliament has approved") described later in the passage.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always scan the surrounding sentences for repeated or paraphrased information — the answer to an earlier blank is often confirmed or echoed later in the passage.

• "Has/have + V3" is the standard Present Perfect Tense structure used to describe a recently completed action with present relevance.

Following in the footsteps of France, Italy has ________(1)________ a new tax to be ________(2)________ on large tech companies, a move that is likely to put more strain on the country's relations with the USA. The Italian parliament has approved a 3% digital tax on some digital revenue of technology companies that make over $831 million in global revenue, including at least $6 million in Italy. The tax ________(3)________ similar to the one France implemented earlier this year, which has attracted ________(4)________ criticism from the USA. According to a report in The Epoch Times, dozens of countries are working on proposals to change corporate tax schemes to ________(5)________ money from tech firms that have users across the world, such as Facebook and Google's parent company Alphabet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. levied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"a new tax to be ________ on large tech companies"**.

• "Levied" is the standard collocation used with "tax" — the verb "to levy" means to impose or collect a tax, fee, or fine. The passive infinitive "to be levied on" is the exact, standard expression used for imposing a tax on an entity.
◦ Example: A new import duty was levied on luxury goods entering the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "crossed" does not collocate with "tax"; it means to move across something, which is meaningless here.

• Option 3: "placed" is grammatically possible but not the standard, precise collocation used with "tax" in formal/economic writing, unlike "levied".

• Option 4: "exercised" means to make use of a right or power, and does not collocate with "tax" in this way.

NOTE

• Fixed collocations with "tax" frequently tested by SSC: levy a tax, impose a tax, collect a tax, evade a tax, exempt from tax.

• "Levy" can also function as a noun meaning "a sum of money that is paid to a government" — e.g. "a new levy on plastic bags".

Following in the footsteps of France, Italy has ________(1)________ a new tax to be ________(2)________ on large tech companies, a move that is likely to put more strain on the country's relations with the USA. The Italian parliament has approved a 3% digital tax on some digital revenue of technology companies that make over $831 million in global revenue, including at least $6 million in Italy. The tax ________(3)________ similar to the one France implemented earlier this year, which has attracted ________(4)________ criticism from the USA. According to a report in The Epoch Times, dozens of countries are working on proposals to change corporate tax schemes to ________(5)________ money from tech firms that have users across the world, such as Facebook and Google's parent company Alphabet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. is.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank fills the sentence **"The tax ________ similar to the one France implemented earlier this year", which describes a present state of resemblance** between the Italian tax and the French tax.

• Since the subject "the tax" is singular and the statement describes a general, current fact (a state of being, not an action in progress), the Simple Present Tense verb "is" is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "are" is incorrect because the subject "the tax" is singular and requires a singular verb.

• Option 3: "were" is incorrect because it is a past tense form, but the sentence describes a present state of similarity, not a past one.

• Option 4: "have" is incorrect because it cannot be followed directly by an adjective ("similar") in this construction, and also does not agree with the singular subject "the tax" (which would require "has", not "have", in any case).

NOTE

• Subject-verb agreement: a singular subject ("the tax") always takes a singular verb ("is/was/has"), never a plural one ("are/were/have").

• The adjective "similar" is typically followed by the preposition "to" ("similar to"), a common collocation tested by SSC.

The Italian parliament has approved a 3% digital tax on some digital revenue of technology companies that make over $831 million in global revenue, including at least $6 million in Italy. The tax ________(3)________ similar to the one France implemented earlier this year, which has attracted ________(4)________ criticism from the USA. According to a report in The Epoch Times, dozens of countries are working on proposals to change corporate tax schemes to ________(5)________ money from tech firms that have users across the world, such as Facebook and Google's parent company Alphabet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. severe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"which has attracted ________ criticism from the USA"**, describing the intensity of criticism the tax has received.

• "Severe" means very great, harsh, or intense, and collocates naturally with "criticism" to indicate strong disapproval — matching the context of the passage, which describes the tax as straining USA-Italy relations.
◦ Example: The new policy attracted severe criticism from opposition parties.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "mild" means gentle or not severe, which contradicts the context of a tax that is "likely to put more strain" on relations between the two countries.

• Option 3: "critical" is redundant and awkward here ("critical criticism"), and is not the standard collocation used with "criticism".

• Option 4: "firm" typically collocates with words like "decision" or "stance", not with "criticism", and does not convey the required sense of intensity.

NOTE

• Common intensity-adjective collocations tested by SSC: severe criticism/pain/shortage, harsh criticism, strong opposition, fierce competition.

• Context clues (here, "put more strain on relations") often signal whether a positive or negative-intensity word is required.

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Following in the footsteps of France, Italy has ________(1)________ a new tax to be ________(2)________ on large tech companies, a move that is likely to put more strain on the country's relations with the USA. The Italian parliament has approved a 3% digital tax on some digital revenue of technology companies that make over $831 million in global revenue, including at least $6 million in Italy. The tax ________(3)________ similar to the one France implemented earlier this year, which has attracted ________(4)________ criticism from the USA. According to a report in The Epoch Times, dozens of countries are working on proposals to change corporate tax schemes to ________(5)________ money from tech firms that have users across the world, such as Facebook and Google's parent company Alphabet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. capture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"proposals to change corporate tax schemes to ________ money from tech firms that have users across the world"**.

• "Capture" here means to succeed in obtaining or claiming (revenue/value) — it precisely conveys the idea of tax schemes being redesigned so that countries can claim/collect tax revenue generated by large tech firms from users located within their borders, even though the firms are not physically based there.
◦ Example: The new proposals aim to capture tax revenue from digital companies based on where their users are located, not just where the company is headquartered.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "take" is too generic and informal for this formal, economic-policy context; it does not carry the specific sense of "successfully claiming a share of" revenue.

• Option 2: "remove" means to take something away entirely, which contradicts the intended meaning of collecting/claiming a share of the money, not eliminating it.

• Option 3: "seize" implies forceful or abrupt confiscation, which is too strong and inaccurate for the description of formal tax-policy proposals.

NOTE

• The word "capture" is frequently used in economic and policy writing to mean "to successfully claim a share of (value, revenue, or market)" — e.g. "capture market share", "capture value".

• This passage reflects real debates on digital/tech taxation, where countries seek to tax revenue based on user location rather than company headquarters — a concept often called "destination-based taxation".
